title: Types of AI
tagline: Where does an AI's skill come from? Compare written rules, learned scores, and a neural network on one board.
card_blurb: One tic-tac-toe board, three real mechanisms. 1a exposes eight hand-written rules and checks the resulting policy. 1b learns a value table in visible game bursts. 1c visibly runs a fresh copy of the 1b algorithm for 20,000 seeded games, freezes its current estimates as examples, then trains shared neural-network weights. It reports positions kept out of training separately from a reproducible play comparison. Ultimate tic-tac-toe remains an optional advanced extension.
description: **Types of AI** is a single-file, phone-first tic-tac-toe demo with accessible tabs for **1a Rules-based intelligence**, **1b Machine learning**, and **1c Neural networks**. The rules tab shows every hand-written condition behind a move and verifies its policy by exhaustive search. The machine-learning tab begins with a zero-filled afterstate value table, trains through visible bursts, preserves eras for comparison, and uses the same verifier for any unbeatable claim. The neural-network tab visibly creates learning examples by running a fresh copy of the 1b algorithm through 20,000 seeded games, then freezes that run’s current table estimates. Related board positions stay together when some are kept out of training, and shared weights learn to approximate the frozen examples. The page explains mean squared error and compares each checkpoint on the same independent sample of random games. During play the network evaluates legal afterstates with its own weights; it does not consult the frozen table or a solver. The demo does not call this network unbeatable. Held-out error is evidence for the defined split, not a guarantee of generalisation. Ultimate tic-tac-toe is available as an optional advanced representation-limit extension, not as the neural-network stage. The demo works offline with no runtime network requests, accounts, or AI service and includes a printable guide.
